To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a trace gas sensor based QEPAS with a quantum cascade (QC) laser operating at 4550 nm as excitation source was realized.
we have demonstrated the first trace-gas sensor based on quantum cascade laser excitation of a gas sample and quartz-enhanced photo-acoustic spectroscopy.
the detection limits in the fundamental molecular bands of N2O, CO, CH4, and H2O were improved by a factor of 2-5 by employing a quantum cascade laser as excitation source.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of gas sensor based on the quartz-enhanced photo-acoustic effect (QEPAS) and a quantum cascade laser (QCL).
the development of a novel trace-gas sensor based on QEPAS.
the design, development, and application of a novel trace gas sensor based upon quartz-enhanced photo acoustic spectroscopy (QEPA) with a quantum cascade (QC) laser.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented sensor is the most sensitive gas detection system ever demonstrated in the 4-5 μm spectral region.
QEPAS is a very promising technique for trace gas detection in the fundamental molecular bands region.
QEPAS is a promising technique for the detection of trace gases in the mid-infrared spectral region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the QEPAS technique can be successfully applied for the detection of trace gases with a sensitivity comparable to other techniques such as cavity ring-down spectroscopy and photoacoustic spectroscopies.
we have demonstrated that the sensitivity of QEPAS can be improved significantly by operating the laser at the fundamental absorption band of the target gas. Proc. SPIE 10111, 24
the sensitivity and detection limit for the detection of CO in the 4.55-μm range is about two orders of magnitude better than those reported previously.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the detection of trace gases in the fundamental molecular vibration region by QEPAS is feasible, even for gases that have a low absorption strength.
